---
title: "How do I compare two measurements matched by the same subject?"
---

## Question

How do I compare two measurements matched by the same subject?

## Decide which method fits

Pair records using an actual subject ID; compare differences within matched pairs; use a paired t test only after matching the before and after measurements.

## Worked example: sleep

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("sleep")
first <- subset(d, group==1, select=c(ID, extra))
second <- subset(d, group==2, select=c(ID, extra))
matched <- merge(first, second, by="ID", suffixes=c("_1","_2"))
fit <- ru_apply("paired_t", matched,
                x="extra_1", y="extra_2", paired=TRUE, confidence=.95)
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$p.value))
```

Each pair comes from the same identified person. The test concerns the average within-person difference, not a difference between unrelated groups. Matching by row position without checking IDs can silently produce false pairs.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("paired_t", your_matched_data, x="before", y="after", paired=TRUE, confidence=.95)
```

If records are from different people and are independent, consider two_sample_t rather than a paired procedure.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("paired_t")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
